description: Weekly brief of buying asks. Use this when the user wants a short summary of the last 7 days of people asking for a service, such as "weekly brief for SEO audit" or "did anyone ask for bookkeeping this week?". To list people asking for a replacement for any tool, pass the service "alternative" alone, with no keywords. Pass service and optionally keywords and sources. Returns one summary line, counts by source and by day, and the top 10 posts with link, date, short quote, score, label, reason and reply_angle. Same rules and sources as find_buying_intent, fixed to 7 days. A quiet week returns no_data. Reddit is not searched.

keywords.description: Optional extra words a post must also contain, such as "shopify" or "small business" (up to 5). Every keyword must appear in a post, so a long list returns little. Leave it out for a first look and add one word only to narrow

service.description: The paid service you sell, in plain words, such as "SEO audit", "bookkeeping" or "logo design". Not a company and not a person. Words are matched as written, so try the person form too (for example "bookkeeper")

sources.description: Which public sources to read: hackernews (comments and Ask HN), github (open and closed issues) and stackexchange. Default is all three. Leave one out to skip it, for example stackexchange when it is rate limited

name: weekly_brief

intent_score.description: 0 to 100 from the rules in how_scored. 40 or more is intent; a casual complaint scores 15

quote.description: A quote of the ask, under 15 words

reason.description: One line naming the rules that matched

reply_angle.description: One line on what to reply. It never names the tool or the subject, so open the link to read it. Picked by rule from the strongest cue: thanks (check the thread first), a budget, a hire, a named friction, an alternative, a recommendation, or a complaint with no ask

url.description: Link to the post. For Stack Exchange this link is also the CC BY-SA attribution

title: Weekly brief of buying asks
